_comment: What one Performance+ probe measurement must record for it to count.
The G0 gate exists because Worker vs Window, the transport, the frame
clock and the WebView host shape are unresolved, and a design that picks
one without device evidence has picked it by preference. This file is the
other half of that discipline: it says what evidence looks like, so a run
cannot be accepted because it was the only one anybody did.
Two rules shape every required field below:
1. A MISSING FIELD REJECTS THE RUN, not the record. A record that lost
its thermal state is not a slightly worse sample; it is a sample
nobody can tell apart from one taken on a hot phone, and averaging it
in is how a thermally-throttled arm wins.
2. EVERY DIMENSION IS RECORDED EVEN WHEN IT IS NOT THE VARIABLE. A run
that varies transport still records agent, clock and layout, because
'one variable at a time' can only be checked against records that say
what all the other variables were.
Enforced by tools/apple-probe-decision/decide.py. These are the
sentences from the design that would otherwise live only in prose, and
prose does not fail a build.
decision_rules._seed_comment: Fixed so a decision is reproducible from the same raw data. A tool that returns a different winner on a second run is not evidence.

primary_metric.name: input_to_present_p95_ms
primary_metric._comment: The number the lane exists to improve. Secondary metrics are recorded and reported but never override it.

_held_fixed_comment: Rule 2 above says every dimension is recorded even when it is not the
variable, 'because one variable at a time can only be checked against
records that say what all the other variables were'. Recording them was
only half of that sentence: until this list existed, decide.py held
fixed the four entries of `variables` and nothing else, so twenty
samples taken on an iPhone 11 at 4 MiB and twenty taken on an iPhone 15
at 4 KiB were the two arms of a transport comparison and the tool named
a winner. Every field here is part of the condition a comparison is
made under, so two records that differ in one of them are not two
thermal_state is deliberately NOT here. It varies across the samples of
a single arm by nature -- a thirty-minute soak passes through several --
so holding it fixed would split every arm into fragments below the
sample floor and reject everything. It stays required and reported.
jit_enabled is here because of A24: Lockdown Mode disables JIT for web
content, so 'WebContent has JIT' is a device state to probe, not an
invariant to assume. Two otherwise identical records that differ in it

combination_rules.reason: a Window agent has no Window to relay to; a record saying so mislabelled which context owned the socket

_enum_comment: The enums are closed on purpose. An unrecognised value is a run that
measured something this decision cannot name, and silently bucketing it
with the nearest known value is how a hybrid transport's numbers end up

_comment: The G0 choices. A decision may be made for one of these only when the
matrix isolates it.
transport_owner joined this list on 2026-09-09, after the 2026-09-07
adversarial review turned A22 from settled into falsified. `WebSocket`
is exposed to Workers, so a Window relay is not a requirement of the
API -- it is a consequence of a Worker blocked in Atomics.wait being
unable to service its own socket. That admits a third topology nobody
had considered, an I/O Worker that owns the socket and notifies the
content Worker. Without this dimension all three record as
agent=dedicated_worker, transport=loopback_websocket, which does not
merely lose a label: it pools two different architectures into one arm
of a comparison against scheme_request.
variables.agent: Where content JavaScript runs: the Window, or a Dedicated Worker. A22 is why this no longer implies who owns the socket -- see transport_owner. A21 is why a Window win is no longer excluded on capability grounds alone: synchronous XHR is a second public blocking primitive, so `Window cannot serve synchronous content` is a claim the capability gate settles, not a premise.
variables.transport: The wire mechanism: a loopback WebSocket, a custom-scheme binary request, a synchronous-XHR RPC, or a hybrid split by direction. sync_xhr_rpc is here because A21 named it as an arm of the pure-transport gate; leaving it out of the enum would have made the one arm that tests A21 unrecordable.
variables.transport_owner: Which JavaScript context owns the transport: the same context that runs content (same_context), a Window relaying for it (window_relay), or a second I/O Worker (io_worker). This is what tells the five arms of measurement gate 2 apart.
variables.clock: Worker rAF where feature detection finds it, Window rAF relayed, or a host CADisplayLink relayed.
